strings.name: Zadie Smith
strings.summary: Drawing on families and neighborhoods in northwest London, Smith explores class, migration, race and intimacy in novels including White Teeth and NW. Her fiction extends from the contemporary city into history, alongside plays, stories and essays. Dead and Alive considers public life through art and literature; she discussed its translations in Barcelona in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explores diverse cities, class and identity through White Teeth and criticism, as an important cross-cultural voice in contemporary English-language literature.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Northwest London; her mother is Jamaican and her father English.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied English literature at the University of Cambridge, where she earned her degree.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Many voices of urban life
strings.highlights.h1.text: White Teeth and NW use families and neighborhoods to portray conflicts and connections in diverse London.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Thinking beyond the novel
strings.highlights.h2.text: Essays, stories and the Chaucer adaptation The Wife of Willesden broaden her literary forms.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discussed essays in Barcelona
strings.timeline.t1.text: Presented new translations of Dead and Alive at the CCCB and discussed writing and ways of thinking.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Published Dead and Alive
strings.timeline.t2.text: The collection approaches contemporary public questions through art, literature and everyday experience.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published her first historical novel
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Fraud examines empire, class and truth around a Victorian trial.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published Swing Time
strings.timeline.t4.text: Two girls' connection to dance explores friendship, class and international relationships.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Published NW
strings.timeline.t5.text: Used varied narrative forms to follow diverging lives in northwest London.
strings.timeline.t6.title: On Beauty appeared
strings.timeline.t6.text: Its university families and cultural conflicts won the Orange Prize for Fiction the following year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: White Teeth published
strings.timeline.t7.text: Her first novel won several debut awards and quickly brought her international attention.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Student manuscript secured a contract
strings.timeline.t8.text: White Teeth sparked a rights auction before completion, as writing developed alongside her Cambridge studies.
